text: . President Droupadi Murmu has said the younger generation of the country has much to learn from the courage and skills of ancient maritime traders. Addressing Bali Jatra Festival 2026 at Kataka in Odisha, she urged people to draw inspiration from the past to shape the present and build a brighter future. The President said that the Bali Jatra is a unique festival which celebrates the glorious history of Odisha. She said that the merchants from Odisha used to travel to distant lands to engage in trade and commerce.President Murmu said that through trade, they accomplished many significant things for the country. She said, they discovered new maritime routes and strengthened international relations. The President noted that the historical connection between Odisha and Bali can be transformed into modern commercial and cultural cooperation. She also expressed happiness that cultural troupes from Indonesia are participating in this year’s Bali Jatra and that the Odisha Festival is being celebrated in Bali, featuring Odisha’s dance and music, handlooms, handicrafts, and traditional cuisine.The President expressed confidence that such cultural exchanges will strengthen the historical ties between India and Indonesia. She said, India’s stature on the international stage has grown. While there is unrest in many parts of the world and instability in the global economy, India’s economy continues to remain strong. This is a promising indicator of our journey toward becoming Viksit Bharat, she said.

. Israel Defense Forces (IDF) and Israel Security Agency (ISA) had eliminated Naim Muhammad Ashour Abu Nahal, the head of Hamas’ Internal Security Apparatus, in an aerial strike. Announcing the operation, the IDF and ISA, in a joint statement, said that Abu Nahal was a senior Hamas figure who had held several key positions within the organisation’s internal security apparatus, including deputy head and head of its Northern District. According to the joint announcement, Abu Nahal had advanced attacks against Israeli troops and civilians during the war and had worked to restore the capabilities of terrorist organisations in the Gaza Strip. The Israeli agencies further alleged that he had systematically violated the ceasefire, adding that the aerial strike was carried out to remove the threat he posed.

. The Supreme Court has refused to grant interim bail to activists Sharjeel Imam and Umar Khalid at present in the 2020 northeast Delhi riots conspiracy case. They had challenged a Delhi High Court order denying them bail in a UAPA case related to the alleged conspiracy behind the February 2020 northeast Delhi riots.A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana issued notice to the Delhi Police and sought its response. It said it would hear the police before considering the prayer for interim bail. The top court also directed that the matter be placed before the CJI on the administrative side for constitution of a three-judge bench for consideration.

. In the United Arab Emirates, 11 people were killed in a collision between a passenger bus and a truck on Al Watan Road in Ras Al Khaimah city. The UAE Ministry of Interior today said that emergency response teams rushed to the accident site and carried out rescue and emergency medical operations in coordination with ambulance crews, civil defence teams and other relevant authorities. The ministry said an investigation has been launched to determine the cause of the accident.The Indian Consulate in Dubai has confirmed that the fatalities also included some Indian nationals. The Indian diplomatic post has expressed condolences to the grieving families. The consulate has reached out to the bereaved families and is closely working with the local authorities to provide all possible assistance and support. It has also shared a 24/7 toll-free helpline number: 800-46342.

. In Men’s Cricket, the first Test between New Zealand and India ended in a draw. In reply to India’s 720 for 9 in first innings, New Zealand made 239 for 5 in their second innings. Akashvani correspondent reports that resuming the final day at 119 for two, Kiwis lost two well-set overnight batters in Devon Conway and Rachin Ravindra. However, Daryl Mitchell and Glenn Phillips stood firm for 43 overs as New Zealand batted out 120 overs in their second innings to salvage a draw in the first Test today.India had taken a 352-run first-innings lead after posting their highest-ever Test total in New Zealand, but could manage only three of the eight wickets they needed on the final day. The Visitors declared their first innings at a record 720 for 9, taking a huge lead of 352 runs over New Zealand’s first-innings score of 368. India also created two major records and became the first team to have their top five batters score 80 or more runs in the same innings.They also became the first team to build partnerships of 50 or more runs for each of the first seven wickets. For Visitors, KL Rahul played a key role at the top of the order. He became the first Indian opener to score a Test century in all four SENA countries South Africa, England, New Zealand and Australia.

. In Mens Cricket, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi created history by breaking the world records for the fastest century and double century in List A cricket as India ‘A’ defeated the United Arab Emirates (UAE) by seven wickets in a group stage match of the Asia Cup Rising Stars tournament in Doha, Qatar. Chasing a target of 250 runs set by the UAE, India ‘A’ comfortably reached the target in just 14.2 overs for the loss of three wickets. Vaibhav smashed 204 runs off just 53 balls, reaching his century in only 28 deliveries to register the fastest hundred in List A cricket. The young batting prodigy then went on to complete his double century in just 52 balls with 28 sixes and seven fours, setting another world record for the fastest double century. He was also named Player of the Match for his match-winning performance. Earlier, opting to bat, UAE posted 249 runs for 8 in their allotted 50 overs. Harpreet Singh Bhatia was the top scorer with 130 runs. For India ‘A’, Arshad Khan picked up four wickets.

. Thirty-seven new houses are set to be constructed in Sri Lanka’s plantation communities under India’s ongoing housing assistance programme. The foundation stones were laid at Kiriwanakettiya and Kobowela Estates in Kalutara District by Sri Lanka’s Minister of Plantations and Community Infrastructure, K.V. Samantha Vidyarathna, along with officials from the Indian High Commission and Members of Parliament.The construction is part of the fourth phase, second stage, of the Indian Housing Project, which is building 4,700 homes across plantation areas in Sri Lanka. The project aims to improve living conditions for plantation families, many of whom have faced longstanding housing challenges.India’s housing assistance remains an important part of its development partnership with Sri Lanka, particularly in supporting communities and improving access to better living conditions. The initiative reflects the people-centred dimension of India-Sri Lanka cooperation, with development assistance reaching communities at the grassroots level.

. Today is the International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women. The day is observed on November 25 every year to raise awareness about violence against women and girls and call for an end to abuse and discrimination. This year, the United Nations marks the day under the theme, UNITE to End Violence Against Women and Girls: Ensure Justice, Protect Survivors, End Impunity.The theme highlights the need for stronger justice systems, safe reporting mechanisms, better support services for survivors and accountability for perpetrators. It also recognizes that violence against women takes place in homes, workplaces, public spaces and online.According to the UN, one in three women worldwide experiences physical or sexual violence during her lifetime. However, many survivors still struggle to access justice, protection and support due to fear, social stigma, discrimination and weak institutional responses.

. President Droupadi Murmu today called for strengthening scientific research, evidence-based evaluation and patient safety to enhance the credibility of homoeopathy. She said healthcare and education must remain the two important pillars of India’s journey towards Viksit Bharat by 2047.Addressing the National Scientific Convention on Homoeopathy at Dr Abhinna Chandra Homoeopathic Medical College and Hospital in Bhubaneswar on the last day of her two-day visit to home state Odisha, the President emphasised that the future of Homoeopathy must be guided by scientific integrity, rigorous research and clinical evidence.She called for multicentric clinical studies, systematic research, transparent reporting and greater collaboration among medical institutions. Highlighting the transformative role of Artificial Intelligence, digital health technologies and modern research, she urged Homoeopathic institutions to embrace technological advancements and contemporary teaching methods.The President also stressed that compassion, patient safety and human dignity must remain at the heart of healthcare. Emphasising the importance of rural healthcare and education, she said greater attention must be given to improving access to these essential services for people in villages. She expressed confidence that the convention would promote scientific dialogue, institutional partnerships and a new generation of competent and socially responsible healthcare professionals.

. The first-ever BIMSTEC Under-23 athletics championships will begin today at the iconic Kalinga Stadium in Bhubaneswar. The three-day track and field competition will feature six nations and 32 medal events. It will bring together more than 200 athletes from six nations – Bangladesh, Bhutan, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Myanmar and host India.The BIMSTEC meet is being conducted by the Athletics Federation of India (AFI) under the auspices of the Union Ministry of External Affairs and Union Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports in collaboration with its counterparts in Odisha. India is fielding a 70-member contingent, chosen from the recently concluded Under-23 Indian Open in Ludhiana and the Junior nationals in Chennai. The 32 medal events, evenly distributed among men and women, will see 210 athletes in action.

. S&P Global has projected India to be one of the fastest-growing economies in the Asia-Pacific region in 2027. The agency expects India’s economy to grow by 7 per cent in both the current fiscal year and the next fiscal year, ending March 2028.In its Economic Outlook Asia-Pacific Q1 2027 report, the agency said India’s growth in the June and September quarters was driven by robust goods exports, government-led investment spending and strong household consumption, supported by buoyant credit growth.The global firm also highlighted India’s growing integration into global supply chains, noting that export performance had benefited from trade diversification and the country’s expanding role in global manufacturing. Electronics, engineering goods and chemicals were among the sectors that recorded particular strength.S&P Global projects inflation to average 5.3 per cent in the current fiscal year ending March 2027, with risks tilted to the upside. However, it expects inflation to ease to 4.7 per cent in the fiscal year ending March 2028.Against this backdrop, the agency expects the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to raise policy rates by a further 25 basis points in December. It also said the likelihood of another rate hike in early 2027 had increased.

. World Fisheries Day is being observed today. The day aims to highlight the importance of sustainable fisheries and aquaculture in ensuring food and nutritional security, generating livelihoods and maintaining ecological balance. The observance traces its origins to 1997, when representatives from 18 countries gathered in New Delhi to establish the World Fisheries Forum. The initiative aimed to promote responsible fishing practices and safeguard the rights and interests of fishing communities.The theme for World Fisheries Day 2026 is “Empowering People for Change: Advancing Decent Work in Fisheries and Aquaculture, Particularly for Youth and Women.” The theme highlights the need to promote decent employment opportunities, empower women and young people, and ensure inclusive and sustainable growth across the fisheries and aquaculture sectors.India is the world’s second-largest fish-producing country, accounting for nearly eight per cent of global fish production. The country has made significant progress in the sector over the past decade. India’s total fish production has more than doubled, rising from 96 lakh tonnes to 195 lakh tonnes last year. The fisheries sector is an important pillar of the Indian economy, supporting the livelihoods of millions of people. A coordinated approach involving all stakeholders is aimed at further strengthening the sector, with a focus on increasing fish production, boosting exports and creating more livelihood opportunities.

. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over Keralam, Mahe, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal during the next two days. The Met Department predicted thunderstorms accompanied by lightning over Andhra Pradesh and Lakshadweep till tomorrow. According to IMD, thunderstorm accompanied with Lightning is likely to prevail over South Interior Karnataka till tomorrow. IMD has said that a gradual fall in minimum temperature by three to four degress Celsius is expected over East India during the next two days.

. In Hockey, India thrashed China 6-2 in their league-stage encounter of the Women’s Asian Champions Trophy in Bhopal. For India, Deepika led the charge with a brilliant hat-trick, while Lalremsiami, Neha and Sakshi Rana netted one goal each. Hong Youngeun and Chen Tong scored for China. This was India’s fourth consecutive victory in the tournament, following their earlier wins over Thailand, Malaysia and South Korea.Earlier in the day, Japan secured a convincing 3-1 victory over Malaysia in their league-stage match, while South Korea also registered a 1-nil win against Thailand.

. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Karaikal, and Andaman and Nicobar Islands tomorrow.The Met Department has also predicted thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds over Kerala, Mahe and Lakshadweep during the next two days. Similar conditions are expected over Assam, Meghalaya, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, and Tripura tomorrow.Meanwhile, the weather agency has forecast mist and shallow fog at most places of Delhi during the morning hours tomorrow.The air quality in Delhi-NCR is in the ‘ Very Poor’ category. According to the Central Pollution Control Board, Delhi’s Air Quality Index was recorded at 303 as of 7 PM today.

. India strongly condemned the attack on one of the towers of the financial district in Riyadh yesterday, as well as continued attacks targeting civilian, economic and energy infrastructure in Saudi Arabia. In a statement, the Ministry of External Affairs said that these attacks seriously endanger civilian lives, violate the sovereignty of Saudi Arabia, and undermine regional security and stability. The Ministry informed that two Indians are among those injured in the attack on Riyadh’s financial district.It said that the Embassy of India in Riyadh is providing all possible assistance to the injured and their families. New Delhi called for immediate cessation of such attacks. It reiterated its firm solidarity with the people and Government of Saudi Arabia. It reaffirmed unwavering support to Saudi Arabia in safeguarding its sovereignty, territorial integrity, and the security and safety of its citizens and residents. India expressed hope that peace and normalcy will return to the region at the earliest.

. The 45th Indian International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026 will begin tomorrow at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi. Talking to media, Chairman of India Trade Promotion Organisation, Jawed Ashraf said that this year the focus is on three key aspects that are enhancing the visitor experience, showcasing innovations and highlighting India’s rich heritage. He said that visitors can book tickets online through the IITF 2026 mobile application, which is integrated with the DMRC’s Sarthi app. Mr Ashraf informed that shuttle bus services will operate from several metro stations, including Mandi House, connecting visitors to all entry gates of the venue. Visitors can also reach Bharat Mandapam through app-based taxis, private vehicles and public transport. He added that parking facilities for around three thousand vehicles have been arranged, along with designated waiting areas for app-based taxis. Special facilities, including wheelchair assistance will also be available for senior citizens to ensure a comfortable and convenient experience.

. Market participants will focus on geopolitical developments, the final leg of the corporate earnings season, foreign portfolio investor (FPI) flows, commodity price movements and currency fluctuations for cues next week.Indian equity markets will remain closed on Tuesday on account of Gurpurab, the birth anniversary of Sri Guru Nanak Dev. Meanwhile, on the primary market front, two mainboard IPOs are scheduled to open for subscription, while two companies are set to make their stock market debut.In the United States, investors will closely monitor the upcoming Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) inflation data, along with the second estimate of third-quarter GDP growth. Meanwhile, market participants will also keep a close watch on the Bank of Korea’s upcoming monetary policy decision for cues on the global interest rate outlook.

. The National Testing Agency (NTA) has informed that tomorrow is the final date to register for the first session of the JEE (Main) examination, with the inclusion of a late fee. In a post on social media, the NTA said that 15 lakh 73 thousands 18 registration forms have been submitted so far, of which more than 13 lakh 96 thousands 7 candidates have successfully completed their fee payment.

. Saudi Arabia and the Houthis today exchanged threats of hitting each other’s ports along the Red Sea. A day after the 2nd attack in less than a week targeting the PIF tower in Riyadh, the Saudi-led coalition issued a threat warning for the Houthi-controlled Yemeni seaport of Hodeidah. It asked civilians to evacuate the port for their safety.The Houthis, in return, announced that Jeddah and all Saudi ports along the Red Sea coast will be targets if the Saudis carry out their threat to bomb Hodeidah. They warned the employees, workers and anyone near these ports to evacuate immediately and stay away, calling on all shipping companies to move their ships out of those ports immediately.Hours after issuing the threat, the spokesperson for the Saudi-led military coalition posted on X that they targeted operational capabilities at Hodeidah port and destroyed a number of targets in Saada and Amran governorates – areas under the Houthi control in Yemen. The Saudis also reported incoming drone attacks in the Saudi Eastern Province.The Saudi Civil Defence had yesterday posted that one of the towers in the Financial Center in Riyadh was targeted in a Houthi attack resulting in 11 injuries. The attack was carried out using drones and the Saudis had said that the attack would be responded to firmly. The Public Investment Fund Tower in Riyadh is one of the tallest buildings in Saudi Arabia and was attacked earlier on 19th November.The Indian Embassy in Riyadh confirmed that the injured also included two Indian nationals. Condemning the attack, India’s Ministry of External Affairs said that the Indian Mission is providing all possible assistance to the injured and their families.

. In Hockey, India defeated China 6-2 in their league-stage match of the Women’s Asian Champions Trophy in Bhopal last night. For India, Deepika scored a brilliant hat-trick, while Lalremsiami, Neha and Sakshi Rana scored one goal each. Hong Youngeun and Chen Tong scored for China.This was India’s fourth consecutive victory in the tournament. Earlier, India defeated Malaysia 4-1, South Korea 2-1 and Thailand 7-0. In other matches yesterday, Japan beat Malaysia 3-1, while South Korea defeated Thailand 1-0.India and Japan are currently at the top of the points table with 12 points each. Having already secured a place in the semi-finals, India will now turn their attention to their final league-stage encounter against Japan today. The match will begin at 7 PM.

. Most Asian stock market indices ended on a positive note today, led by chipmakers and technology companies following a rebound in the sector on Wall Street. Taiwan’s Taiex skyrocketed 9%, South Korea’s Kospi surged over 6.3%, Japan’s Nikkei 225 gained 3.9%, China’s Shanghai Composite added almost 0.%, and Singapore’s Straits Times rose marginally by 0.1%. Conversely, Hong Kong’s Hang Seng dropped over 0.7%.In European markets, Germany’s DAX slipped almost 0.7%, and London’s FTSE 100 dipped 0.1%, when reports last came in.

. On the 2nd day of the ongoing 43rd Indian Oil Servo Surjit Hockey Tournament in Jalandhar, the Punjab Police team secured an impressive victory by defeating CAG Delhi 3-1 in a Pool-C match, today. In Pool-D, the Punjab & Sind Bank (Delhi) team defeated CRPF (Delhi) 1-0. Whereas defending champions Indian Oil advanced to the quarter-finals by defeating Rail Coach Factory, Kapurthala 2-0.Tomorrow, Nov 24th, CAG Delhi will take on Indian Navy Mumbai at 2:15 PM. Indian Air Force will play with CRPF, Delhi at 3:45 PM and the match between PNB Delhi and Army XI Delhi is scheduled at 5:30 PM.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz have reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthen the India-Germany Strategic Partnership, with a focus on expanding cooperation in defence, advanced technologies, trade and investment.The two leaders held a telephone conversation, during which they reviewed progress in bilateral relations and expressed satisfaction over the sustained momentum in engagements between the two countries. As India and Germany mark 75 years of diplomatic relations this year, both leaders reiterated their commitment to deepening cooperation across key sectors.They also noted that the India-European Union Free Trade Agreement will create new opportunities to expand bilateral trade and investment. During the conversation, PM Modi and Mr Merz exchanged views on regional and global developments of mutual interest. They agreed to work closely to promote global peace, stability and a rules-based international order. The two leaders also underscored the importance of continued cooperation at multilateral forums to address contemporary global challenges.

. The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare’s dedicated Health Pavilion at the 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026 in New Delhi is showcasing its flagship health programmes and public healthcare initiatives. The theme of this year’s Health Pavilion is Yuva Bharat, Swasth Bharat, highlights preventive healthcare, healthy lifestyles and youth participation in building a healthier nation. The Pavilion was inaugurated by NITI Aayog Member, Dr M Srinivas, in the presence of Health Secretary, Punya Salila Srivastava.Addressing the gathering, Dr. Srinivas emphasised on preventive healthcare and healthy lifestyle choices to address rising burden of Non-Communicable Diseases (NCDs) and lifestyle-related health conditions. He also highlighted the importance of public awareness, early detection and timely medical intervention in preventing and managing NCDs. Outlining the benefits of Health Pavilion, Dr. Srinivas said that it offers a valuable opportunity for citizens to learn about common health risks, understand preventive measures and familiarise themselves with various Government healthcare programmes and services. He also encouraged visitors to actively participate in the Pavilion’s activities and use the opportunity to enhance their understanding of health and well-being.The Ministry noted that in the Pavilion 39 stalls representing 24 national health programmes and organisations showcase Government’s healthcare initiatives, achievements and services. The Ministry also highlighted that a dedicated TB stall has been established to raise awareness about tuberculosis and TB screening is being conducted using AI-enabled handheld X-ray technology. The Pavilion also included interactive activities, live cpr demonstrations, health awareness sessions and dedicated kids’ zone to engage visitors and promote healthy living. The Ministry said that the Pavilion provides an important platform to connect directly with citizens, showcase the Government’s wide-ranging healthcare initiatives and promote greater public awareness about preventive healthcare, early diagnosis and healthier lifestyles.

. Three major works of India’s literary and intellectual heritage including Kalhana’s Rajatarangini, the Mahabharata and Kautilya’s Arthashastra have been included in UNESCO’s Memory of the World Regional Register for Asia and the Pacific. The decision was taken at the 11th session of the register held in Jakarta, Indonesia. With this recognition, India’s total number of inscriptions in the regional register has risen to six. The three works represent different aspects of India’s knowledge traditions. Rajatarangini is a historical account of Kashmir, the Mahabharata explores Dharma, duty and human values, while Arthashastra deals with governance, diplomacy and statecraft. This recognition is a matter of pride for India’s civilisational continuity, its rich knowledge traditions and its contribution to the world. The development was announced by Member Secretary, Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA),  Dr. Sachchidanand Joshi which played an important role in preparing the nomination dossiers for all three works.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices were trading around one and a half per cent higher during the last hour of trade today. The Sensex climbed 1,350 points to 83,786, while the Nifty rose 392 points to 25,741, when reports last came in.

. In the Indian bullion market today, 24 carat gold plunged nearly 4.4 per cent to 1,23,893 rupees per 10 grams. Meanwhile, silver also tumbled over 4.9 per cent to 1,52,528 rupees per kilogram according to the closing rates of India Bullion and Jewellers Association.

. The combined Index of Core Industries (ICI) registered growth of 10.9 per cent in October on an annual basis driven by strong performance in iron ore, coal, electricity and cement sectors. This is higher than the upwardly revised growth rate of 8.2 per cent recorded in September. According to the provisional estimates released by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry today, six out of nine core sectors recorded positive growth last month. Among these, iron ore production recorded the highest growth at 26.4 per cent. Coal production accelerated by 23.1 per cent, electricity generation increased by 21.6 per cent, cement production gained 15.4 per cent, steel production output grew by 7.3 per cent, and refinery products expanded by 3.4 per cent on an annual basis. However, natural gas production fell by 7.6 per cent, crude oil production dipped by 4.1 per cent, and fertilizer production declined by 12.2 per cent in October on an annual basis.

. In Bangladesh’s Gazipur, garment workers clashed with police today after rejecting the newly announced minimum monthly wage and demanding higher pay.According local media reports, protesting workers blocked the Dhaka-Tangail and Dhaka-Mymensingh highways at several points, including Naojor and Bhogra Bypass, disrupting traffic. Demonstrations were also reported in Tongi and Sreepur. Police fired tear gas and sound grenades to disperse the protesters after some workers reportedly hurled bricks and stones at law enforcement personnel.Gazipur Industrial Police said sporadic protests continued at several locations. By 10 am today, around 20 factories had declared general holidays, while 35 others remained closed indefinitely.The unrest followed the Minimum Wage Board’s decision to raise the minimum monthly wage for garment workers from Taka 12,500 to Taka 17,000.The six-member board finalised the decision through a vote after lengthy negotiations. Four members supported Taka 17,000, while two backed Taka 18,000. While some workers accepted the increase, others said it was insufficient amid rising living costs and continued to demand higher wages.

. The sixth edition of Creative Minds of Tomorrow (CMOT) concluded on a high note at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa. A flagship initiative of the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, this year’s edition brought together 100 aspiring filmmakers for a 48-hour filmmaking challenge, based on the theme Roots & Wings: Honouring our Roots, Embracing our Future.Addressing the closing ceremony yesterday, Additional Secretary in the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, Prabhat, said that CMOT serves as a bridge between young talent and the film industry. Congratulating the participants for completing the 48-hour filmmaking challenge, Mr Prabhat emphasised that the emerging Animation, Visual Effects, Gaming, Comics and Extended Reality (AVGC-XR) sector offers significant opportunities for young creative professionals.Addressing the event, Festival Director of IFFI and filmmaker Ashutosh Gowariker said that filmmaking is a collaborative process and that a film cannot be made by one person alone. Mr Gowariker also encouraged the participants to stay connected with the friends they had made during the challenge and continue working together in their filmmaking journeys.Akashvani correspondent reports that the movie One Last Stop, directed by Mohak Gandhi, won the Best Film award along with a cash prize of five lakh rupees. While, A Little Something, directed by Tamanna Thakur, secured the Runner-up award and received three lakh rupees. Among the individual honours, Siddhi Parkar won the Best Actor award for Shells, while Triasha Manna was adjudged Best Cinematographer for One Last Stop.Jithin S received the Best Scriptwriter award for Shells. Nayan Chotaliya and Manav Agarwal won the Best Editor award for A Little Something. Aswin Ashok was recognised for Best Sound Design for Two Sunsets and Zero Sunrises, while Akshay Anmol Katore received the Best Music Composer award for Neel Machli.Today, the sixth day of IFFI, will witness the much-awaited Lata Mangeshkar Talk: a special tribute to Asha Bhosle and S. Janaki. The discussion will explore the musical legacies of these legendary voices, with K.S. Chithra sharing personal experiences and memories from her association with them. Suhasini Maniratnam will moderate the talk. Another masterclass scheduled for the day is Words Across Borders: Subtitling Across Cultures, featuring Chennai-based subtitlist Rekhs.

. Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, the Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi and Chairman of the Abu Dhabi Executive Council, met with a number of graduates from the first cohort of the Indian Institute of Technology Delhi – Abu Dhabi Campus. Sheikh Khaled congratulated the graduates on their academic achievements, wishing them continued success and excellence in their professional careers. Also present on the occasion were Ms Rima Al Mokarrab (Chairwoman of Tamkeen and executive director of strategic affairs at the Executive Affairs Authority of UAE), Rangan Banerjee (Director, IIT Delhi) and Shantanu Roy (Executive Director, IITD Abu Dhabi).The first batch recently graduated from the institute with an M. Tech. in Energy Transition and Sustainability.  India’s Education Minister Shri Pralhad Joshi presided over the convocation ceremony held in Abu Dhabi on 19th November. The institute is a reflection of the strategic partnership between India and the UAE and the shared vision of the two countries for strengthening bilateral cooperation in higher education, scientific research, and the innovation ecosystem.The decision to establish an IIT in the UAE goes back to February 2022, when Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the then Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi, Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, agreed to establish an Indian Institute of Technology in the United Arab Emirates during their Virtual Summit. In July 2023, an MoU was signed between the Ministry of Education of India, Indian Institute of Technology (IIT Delhi) and Abu Dhabi Department of Education & Knowledge (ADEK) during Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s visit to the UAE in July 2023 to establish IIT Delhi – Abu Dhabi.The IITD – Abu Dhabi campus today offers 6 programmes and includes students and research scholars from across 13 nationalities. Apart from the M. Tech course, the Institute also offers a PhD program in Energy and Sustainability, establishing an early focus on advanced research and innovation in critical sustainability domains. The undergraduate (UG) programs currently include Chemical Engineering, Computer Science and Engineering, Energy Engineering, and Electrical Engineering.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi today said that the government is expanding social security coverage for India’s workforce. In a social media post, Mr Modi shared an article by Vice Chairman of NITI Aayog, Ashok Kumar Lahiri, who writes about the increase in the EPF wage ceiling and its role in bringing more workers under provident fund, pension and insurance protection. In his article, Mr Lahiri also discussed how wider coverage will support employee retention, workforce stability and greater formalisation of employment.

. In Hockey, India thrashed Thailand 7-0 in their league-stage encounter of the Women’s Asian Champions Trophy in Bhopal this evening. Deepika led the charge with a brilliant hat-trick, while Navneet Kaur scored a brace.Mumtaz Khan and skipper Sunelita Toppo also scored one goal each. This was India’s third consecutive victory in the tournament, following their earlier wins over Malaysia and South Korea. With this win, India moved to the top of the points table with nine points.Earlier in the day, Malaysia registered a 3-1 victory over South Korea in their league-stage match, while Japan also secured a convincing 3-1 win against China.

. National Security Advisor Ajit Doval today emphasised the shared maritime and civilisational ties among Indian Ocean littoral states, saying the seas must remain a space that connects nations rather than divides them. Addressing the 8th National Security Advisors’ Meeting of the Colombo Security Conclave in Male, Maldives, Mr Doval called for sustained cooperation among countries in the region to ensure maritime security, regional stability and economic prosperity.He said, the littoral states of the Indian Ocean region share a common maritime space and are connected by civilisational heritage shaped over a long period of history. Mr Doval said the formation of the Colombo Security Conclave in November 2020 was guided by a collective vision to ensure the safety, security and stability of the Indian Ocean Region.He added that the grouping had made considerable progress but still had a long journey ahead. The National Security Advisor also underlined India’s commitment to strengthening the regional grouping, linking the Colombo Security Conclave to New Delhi’s neighbourhood-first policy and its broader MAHASAGAR vision. He noted that the Indian Ocean is important not only for the national security and economic prosperity of countries in the region but also for safeguarding the interests and welfare of their people.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi today said that India’s journey towards Viksit Bharat 2047 is being shaped by sustained reforms and investment across key sectors. Sharing an article by Confederation of Indian Industry CII President R Mukundan in a social media post, Mr Modi said that Mr Mukundan highlighted the foundations laid through infrastructure investment, GST, digital public infrastructure, corporate tax reforms, PLI schemes and trade agreements. In his article, Mr Mukundan further highlighted the importance of government and industry working together as Team Bharat to turn India’s economic potential into lasting prosperity.Prime Minister Modi also noted that India’s civilisational heritage has a growing role in shaping global cultural discourse. In a social media post, he shared an article by Union Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, who wrote about the first SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum and the Indraprastha Communiqué, which sets out a framework for stronger cultural cooperation. In his article, Mr Shekhawat explored how India can take its rich civilisational traditions to a wider global audience through heritage conservation, cultural research, innovation and creative enterprise.

. The nationwide ‘Viksit Bharat Yuva Samvad: Know Your Vote’ campaign has concluded with 536 Yuva Samvads conducted across 31 States and Union Territories. The campaign organised by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports through Mera Yuva Bharat (MY Bharat) reached over one lakh young people and involved more than 5000 Youth Icons. The campaign brought discussions on electoral awareness to colleges and educational institutions across the country. It encouraged young people, particularly first-time voters, to understand their voting rights and electoral procedures and participate responsibly in democracy.The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports said that the campaign witnessed participation by Governors, Union Ministers, State Ministers, Members of Parliament and other public representatives. It added that sports personalities and youth icons from the sporting community also participated in programmes, sharing their experiences and encouraging youth participation in sports.The Yuva Samvads provided young participants with opportunities to seek clarity on electoral procedures, discuss voting rights and civic responsibilities, and interact directly with public representatives and Youth Icons.

. The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) yesterday proposed eliminating additional disclosure requirements for offshore funds, arguing that existing beneficial ownership disclosure norms already provide adequate transparency and oversight. The proposal marks a significant shift from regulations introduced in 2023, when the market regulator tightened scrutiny of offshore investment structures. Under the current framework, offshore funds considered to be at higher risk are required to make enhanced disclosures, including details of their ultimate beneficial owners.The regulator said the proposed changes are aimed at balancing regulatory oversight with ease of doing business while ensuring that capital markets remain attractive to foreign investors. The proposal has been put forward for public consultation, and feedback from market participants is expected before SEBI takes a final decision on amending the framework.

. In Men’s Hockey, the Indian team clinched the three-match 2026 India-New Zealand Century of Sporting Unity Series 1-0 as the third and final match of the tour ended in a 2-2 draw at Lloyd Elsmore Hockey Stadium in Auckland.In the series decider played yesterday, New Zealand took an early lead with Dylan Thomas scoring the first goal in the ninth minute, but India responded with two goals in quick succession. Sanjay converted a penalty corner in the 16th minute to restore parity before Karthi Selvam scored a field goal two minutes later to give the visitors a 2-1 advantage. However, the hosts fought back in the final quarter, with Benji Culhane finding the equaliser in the 55th minute. Neither side managed to find a winner thereafter as the contest ended in a draw, confirming India’s series victory.India had edged New Zealand 3-2 in the opening match while the second match also ended in a 2-2 stalemate.The series also marked 100 years of sporting ties between India and New Zealand, dating back to 1926, when an Indian Army hockey team featuring the legendary Major Dhyan Chand became the first Indian team to tour New Zealand.

. Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSME) Jitan Ram Manjhi today inaugurated the MSME Pavilion at the 45th India International Trade Fair 2026 in New Delhi. On the occasion, Mr Manjhi interacted with artisans and exhibitors at various stalls. He highlighted the importance of khadi as a symbol of country’s rich cultural heritage and traditional craftsmanship. The Minister said that khadi represents country’s traditional industry, entrepreneurship and art. Mr Manjhi also highlighted the PM Vishwakarma Yojana, which covers 18 traditional trades, including barbers, leather artisans, cobblers, garland makers and net weavers.

. In the bullion market, gold and silver prices witnessed a steep decline over the past week as a stronger US dollar and elevated Treasury yields weighed heavily on investor sentiment. For the second week in a row, precious metals remained under pressure as expectations grew that the US Federal Reserve would maintain its hawkish stance to bring inflation back within its 2 per cent target range.At the Multi Commodity Exchange (MCX), Gold futures for December contract plunged 10.9 per cent to settle at 1 lakh 21 thousand 778 rupees per 10 grams during the week. Silver futures for December contract tumbled almost 16.2 per cent to close at 1 lakh 47 thousand 813 rupees per kilogram.Meanwhile, at the Commodity Exchange (COMEX), Gold futures for the December contract plummeted 9.5 per cent during the week to settle at 3515.4 dollars per troy ounce. Silver futures for the December contract nosedived 16.4 per cent over the week to end at 41.07 dollars per troy ounce.

. In Table Tennis, India’s Boys Under-19 team has confirmed its first medal at the ITTF World Youth Championships in Istanbul, Türkiye, after storming into the semifinals. The Indian trio of Priyanuj Bhattacharya, Abhinandh Pradhivadhi and Balamurugan Rajasekaran produced a dominant performance, defeating hosts Türkiye 3-nil in the quarterfinals to seal a place in the last four and guarantee a medal for India. India will now face Chinese Taipei in the semifinals.Meanwhile, Indian Girls’ Under-19 team bowed out in the quarterfinals after suffering a nil-3 defeat to France. Divyanshi, Syndrela and Hansini lost their respective matches.

. At the National Squash Championships 2026, Abhay Singh and Akanksha Salunkhe clinched singles titles. They were crowned the men’s and women’s champions at the National Squash Championships 2026, which concluded at the Otters Club in Mumbai yesterday. This was the 82nd edition of the senior squash nationals.Top seed Abhay Singh, who won a silver medal at the Asian Games 2026, got the better of second seed Veer Chotrani 3-0  in the men’s final. It was a third senior national title for world No. 26 Abhay, who was contesting his fifth consecutive final. Akanksha Salunkhe, meanwhile, came through qualifying to lift her first senior national crown on her third attempt, having lost her two previous finals.

. Union Minister for Railways, Information and Broadcasting, Ashwini Vaishnaw will be on a day’s visit to Tamil Nadu tomorrow. During his visit, the Minister is scheduled to visit the RKTR Forged wheel factory situated at Gummidipoondi near Chennai. He will also visit the TBM facility at Ponneri in Tiruvallur district on the same day.The RKTR has signed the contract for manufacturing and supply of forged wheels under the Atma Nirbhar Bharat scheme by the Ministry of Railways. The total quantity of forged wheels to be supplied will be around 15 lakh 40 thousand wheels over a period of twenty years. The company also manufactures Railway freight wagons, Naval systems and has already delivered 35 vessels for the Indian Navy. They also manufacture electric/hybrid vessels, fast patrol vessels, platform supply vessels, offshore patrol vessels and anchor handling tugs.The Minister will also visit the tunnel boring machine facility at Ponneri, Tiruvallur district. The Primary tunnel boring machine manufacturing and Assembly hub produces metro-sized TBMs used for Chennai Metro Phase 1 & 2, as well as large-diameter mix shields up to 15.62 meters for major road and rail tunnel projects. They are expanding with an additional 12.4-acre manufacturing plant in Kannigaipair in North Chennai to increase production.

Under the theme ‘Vikas Aur Virasat’ (Development and Heritage), women-led Self-Help Groups (SHGs) from Tripura, along with various wings under the Department of Industries and Commerce, are participating in the international trade fair being held in New Delhi.At the 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026, the Tripura Pavilion is showcasing a wide range of products manufactured by the state’s Self-Help Groups, along with an impressive collection of bamboo and cane handicrafts.Tripura Industries and Commerce Minister Santana Chakma visited the state’s stalls and encouraged the women entrepreneurs, appreciating their efforts. She said their contribution is significant in strengthening Tripura’s economy. She further stated that participation in such fairs would help promote products manufactured in Tripura and increase their recognition in the global market.It may be mentioned that Union Minister for Commerce and Industry Piyush Goyal inaugurated the fair on November 13. The exhibition will continue until November 27, with participation from representatives of more than 30 states and Union Territories across the country.

. The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has cautioned investors against relying on unofficial Grey Market Premium (GMP) figures to assess the likely listing prices or expected returns from upcoming Initial Public Offerings (IPOs). In an advisory issued today, SEBI said such pre-listing premium figures are unofficial, unverified and unregulated, as the transactions take place outside the regulated stock market framework, without investor protection or settlement guarantees.SEBI has advised all registered intermediaries and market participants to refrain from publishing or circulating GMP figures. It has also urged investors to avoid GMP-linked transactions and invest in IPOs only through SEBI-registered intermediaries and authorised platforms. The regulator has clarified that investors involved in such transactions will not have access to its or stock exchanges’ grievance redressal mechanisms.

. Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf today warned that Iran will not take any action or enter into negotiations with the United States in order to end the hostilities in West Asia until its seven conditions are met. Iran reiterated its position amid mounting tensions following fresh US sanctions targeting Iranian financial networks. In his remarks at the Iranian Parliament, Ghalibaf reiterated that Tehran’s position remained unchanged and warned that the country was prepared to respond decisively to any hostile moves by its adversaries, adding that Washington’s threats and continued economic pressure against Iran reflected American helplessness. Ghalibaf’s remarks came a day after the US Department of the Treasury announced that it had imposed sanctions on more than two dozen Iranian exchange houses, front companies and key personnel as part of what it described as a sweeping effort to disrupt Iran’s global shadow banking networks.According to the conditions outlined by Iran, Tehran is seeking the lifting of the US naval blockade on Iranian ports, sanctions relief, the release of frozen Iranian funds, an end to hostilities on all fronts and a formal declaration that the war is over.

. Guru Nanak Jayanti, marking the birth anniversary of Guru Nanak Dev Ji, was celebrated with devotion and religious fervour at Gurdwara Nanak Shahi in Dhaka, Bangladesh. The occasion highlighted the timeless teachings of Guru Nanak Dev Ji, including love, equality, compassion, humility, peace and selfless service. Devotees gathered to remember his message of humanity, brotherhood and universal harmony. The celebrations underscored the importance of following the path of truth, spreading kindness and respecting all people, irrespective of their background. The occasion concluded with prayers seeking peace, happiness and prosperity for all.

. The inaugural journey of the Sarayu-Kamala Express from Ayodhya in India to Janakpur Dham in Nepal received a warm welcome upon its arrival at Janakpur Dham today. The train was jointly flagged off by Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah yesterday during the latter’s State Visit to India.The passengers travelling aboard the train were welcomed by Nepal’s Minister for Labour, Youth and Employment, Ramjee Yadav, Madhesh Province Chief Minister Saroj Kumar Yadav, India’s Deputy Chief of Mission and Chargé d’Affaires in Nepal, Dr. Rakesh Pandey, and senior Nepali officials, including representatives of the Nepal Railway Company Limited.A separate programme was also organised at the railway premises in Janakpur Dham to mark the inaugural journey. Speakers appreciated the initiative and highlighted its role in facilitating pilgrimage and further strengthening people-to-people ties between India and Nepal. Following the reception and the programme, the train also undertook its inaugural return journey from Janakpur Dham towards Ayodhya.The rail service connects Ayodhya, associated with Lord Shri Ram, and Janakpur Dham, revered as the birthplace of Mata Sita. The two cities hold special significance in the Ramayana tradition and are important centres of religious and cultural tourism. The new service is expected to facilitate pilgrimage, promote tourism and further strengthen the historic cultural and people-to-people ties between India and Nepal.

On the first day of the 43rd Indian Oil Servo Surjit Hockey Tournament in Jalandhar yesterday, the Pool A match between former champions Indian Oil Mumbai and BSF Jalandhar ended in a 1- 1 draw.Bharat Petroleum registered a hard-fought 2-1 victory over Punjab National Bank (PNB), Delhi, in a Pool-B league match.In Pool-D, the Indian Air Force team delivered an impressive performance, securing victory over Punjab & Sind Bank, Delhi, 2-1.

. The 57th International Film Festival of India, IFFI 2026, in Goa is bringing cinema closer to people through a vibrant blend of films, music, cultural celebrations and creative exchanges. On its sixth day, the festival is celebrating the legacy of legendary voices in Indian music, while also exploring the art of filmmaking and the power of cinema to transcend language barriers.Several special screenings and cultural events are also lined up for the day. Akashvani correspondent reports that one of the highlights of the day is the Lata Mangeshkar Talk, titled The Voice that Echoes Forever – In the Memory of Asha Bhosle and S. Janaki. Acclaimed playback singer K. S. Chithra shared personal memories of her association with the legendary singers. During the session, Chithra also rendered a popular ghazal immortalised by Asha Bhosle, which she described as one of her personal favourites. Talking about S. Janaki, Chithra said that the world only knew her as a singer, but she is also a multi-talented personality.Another key attraction is the masterclass titled Words Across Borders: Subtitling Across Cultures, scheduled for this afternoon. Chennai-based subtitlist Rekhs will explore how subtitles help regional films reach global audiences while preserving their original emotions, humour and cultural nuances. The festival is also showcasing a diverse selection of Indian and international films.The Gujarati film Bhai Band, directed by Manish Saini, is among today’s gala screenings. Film enthusiasts can also revisit two classics of Hindi cinema – Raj Khosla’s C.I.D., marking its centenary, and Yash Chopra’s Kabhi Kabhie, celebrating its golden jubilee. Adding to the festivities, the IFFI Parade, themed Celebrating the Joy of Cinema, will feature colourful floats and cultural performances. The parade will proceed from the Entertainment Society of Goa premises to Kala Academy.

. In Mizoram, three-day Leitlangpui Music Festival is underway in south Mizoram’s Lunglei town, bringing together established musicians, emerging bands and local entrepreneurs to showcase the state’s musical heritage and promote tourism. Organised by the Ministry of Tourism and Mizoram Tourism department, the festival began yesterday at Lena Stadium at Serkawn under the theme “Music Comes Home to Serkawn”. The festival seeks to connect that legacy with contemporary musicians and emerging talent.Addressing the inaugural ceremony, Tourism Minister Lalnghinglova Hmar said music was an inseparable part of Mizoram’s cultural identity and Serkawn held a special place in the state’s musical history. The minister said that the government aimed to take Mizoram’s music and cultural heritage to national and international audiences while creating opportunities for young artists, entrepreneurs and local communities. The festival features performances by established and emerging Mizo musicians.The second day includes a band competition with 10 finalists from Aizawl, Lunglei, Nagaland and Assam, while winners of the previous two editions, Swordtune and Knot, are also scheduled to perform. The final day will feature performances by several Mizo artists and bands, followed by the minister’s address and a fireworks display.
